Perhaps the most important features to help differentiate the EOS R6 V are that it lacks an electronic viewfinder , which the EOS R6 III includes, but it does have in-body image stabilisation , which the C50 lacks.
So photographers wanting a viewfinder are out of luck, but content creators wanting to vlog and quickly create will benefit from the stabilisation, which is lacking in the more cinema-focused C50.
There’s no viewfinder on the Canon EOS R6 V.
Without a viewfinder the R6 V has a more squared design.
With no viewfinder, there is no EVF hump, giving the camera a boxier design compared to the classic SLR shape.
Usefully, the mic and headphone sockets are clear of the rotation of the rear 3” screen, allowing you to fully tilt the screen through 270º without hitting a 3.5mm jack.
Canon EOS R6 V – Viewfinder and screen Again, like its kin, the R6 V uses a 3-inch articulated touchscreen with a 1.62-million-dot resolution .
Without wanting to sound like a broken record, it pales in comparison with the larger 4-inch screen of the Nikon ZR , and it isn’t as bright.

I immediately found myself boosting the screen’s brightness, which obviously means the screen can’t be used to judge exposure correctly, leaving you to trust the camera’s metering features or be a little more reliant on exposure features such as zebra patterning.
The 3-inch screen was not always easy to see in bright sunlight.
This is also where the lack of a viewfinder comes into play; it isn’t only a comfortable, ergonomic device, it is useful and efficient when composing photos and video in bright conditions.
Even checking focus or reviewing footage can be easier through an EVF than on a small screen in bright sunlight.
Indeed like every other camera of this type I review, there is always that awkward moment where reflex kicks in, and I bring it to my eye, forgetting in a moment that there is no viewfinder.
Like the C50, the screen of the EOS R6 V looks dated, simply because the Nikon ZR has reset expectations, and as a photographer, I wish there was an optional EVF.
